articles.title: Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings: State-of-the-art embedding model for agentic RAG and semantic search

articles.author: Bryton Herdes
articles.description:
A BGP “zombie” is essentially a fancy name for a route that has become stuck in the Default-Free Zone (DFZ) of the Internet, potentially due to a missed or lost prefix withdrawal. 

In this post, we will walk through some situations where BGP zombies are more likely to rise from the dead and wreak havoc, how excessive path hunting can contribute to longer periods of impact, and some recommendations and follow-ups we have put together to make them less likely.
articles.title: BGP zombies and excessive path hunting

articles.author: Lucas Pardue
articles.description: HTTP/2 implementations often respond to suspected attacks by closing the connection with an ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM error code. Learn how a common pattern of using Go's HTTP/2 client can lead to unintended errors and the solution to avoiding them.
articles.title: Go and enhance your calm: demolishing an HTTP/2 interop problem

articles.author: Thibault Meunier
articles.description: We propose an open registry format for Web Bot Auth to move beyond IP-based identity. This allows any origin to discover and verify cryptographic keys for bots, fostering a decentralized and more trustworthy ecosystem.
articles.title: Beyond IP lists: a registry format for bots and agents

articles.author: Thibault Meunier
articles.description: As AI agents change how the Internet is used, they create a challenge for security. We explore how Anonymous Credentials can rate limit agent traffic and block abuse without tracking users or compromising their privacy.
articles.title: Anonymous credentials: rate-limiting bots and agents without compromising privacy

articles.author: Lena Heimberger
articles.description: The world is adopting anonymous credentials for digital privacy, but these systems are vulnerable to quantum computers. This post explores the cryptographic challenges and promising research paths toward building new, quantum-resistant credentials from the ground up.
articles.title: Policy, privacy and post-quantum: anonymous credentials for everyone

articles.author: Suleman Ahmad
articles.description: Researchers and practitioners have been studying connections almost as long as the Internet that supports them. Today, Cloudflare’s global network receives millions of connections per second. We explore various characteristics of TCP connections, including lifetimes, sizes, and more.
articles.title: Measuring characteristics of TCP connections at Internet scale

articles.author: Vasilis Giotsas
articles.description: IPv4 scarcity drives widespread use of Carrier-Grade Network Address Translation, a practice in ISPs and mobile networks that places many users behind each IP address, along with their collected activity and volumes of traffic. We introduce the method we’ve developed to detect large-scale IP sharing globally and mitigate the issues that result.
articles.title: One IP address, many users: detecting CGNAT to reduce collateral effects

articles.author: Chris Branch
articles.description: WARP’s initial implementation resembled a VPN that allows Internet access through it. Here’s how we built it – and how you can, too.
articles.title: How to build your own VPN, or: the history of WARP

articles.author: Apoorv Kothari
articles.description: We identified and patched two DDoS vulnerabilities in our QUIC implementation related to packet acknowledgements. Cloudflare customers were not affected. We examine the "Optimistic ACK" attack vector and our solution, which dynamically skips packet numbers to validate client behavior.
articles.title: Defending QUIC from acknowledgement-based DDoS attacks

articles.author: Chris Branch
articles.description: Many products at Cloudflare aren’t possible without pushing the limits of network hardware and software to deliver improved performance, increased efficiency, or novel capabilities such as soft-unicast, our method for sharing IP subnets across data centers. Happily, most people do not need to know the intricacies of how your operating system handles network and Internet access in general. Yes, even most people within Cloudflare. But sometimes we try to push well beyond the design intentions of Linux’s networking stack. This is a story about one of those attempts.
articles.title: So long, and thanks for all the fish: how to escape the Linux networking stack

articles.author: Jocelyn Woolbright
articles.description: Cloudflare mitigated a 12-hour DDoS attack against Moldova's Central Election Commission, blocking over 898 million malicious requests that peaked at 324,333 requests per second. This defense kept critical election infrastructure online and accessible for citizens during a critical parliamentary vote.
articles.title: Helping protect the 2025 Moldova elections

articles.author: Bas Westerbaan
articles.description: Today over half of human-initiated traffic with Cloudflare is protected against harvest-now/decrypt-later with post-quantum encryption. What once was a cool science project, is the new security baseline for the Internet. We’re not done yet: in this blog post we’ll take measure where we are, what we expect for the coming years, and what you can do today.
articles.title: State of the post-quantum Internet in 2025

articles.author: Luke Valenta
articles.description: Cloudflare is launching an experiment with Chrome to evaluate fast, scalable, and quantum-ready Merkle Tree Certificates, all without degrading performance or changing WebPKI trust relationships.
articles.title: Keeping the Internet fast and secure: introducing Merkle Tree Certificates

articles.author: Vasilis Giotsas
articles.description: We present a data-driven framework to quantify cross-layer Internet resilience. We also share a list of measurements with which to quantify facets of Internet resilience for geographical areas.
articles.title: A framework for measuring Internet resilience

articles.title: Announcing Workers automatic tracing, now in open beta

articles.author: David Belson
articles.description: In Q3 2025, we observed Internet disruptions around the world resulting from government directed shutdowns, power outages, cable cuts, a cyberattack, an earthquake, a fire, and technical problems, as well as several with unexplained causes.
articles.title: Online outages: Q3 2025 Internet disruption summary

articles.author: Marwan Fayed
articles.description: The Internet is one big open system composed of many closed boxes — which makes measuring the Internet difficult. In this post we explore Internet measurement as a science.
articles.title: The tricky science of Internet measurement

articles.author: André Jesus
articles.description: Cloudflare Radar has launched a new Top-Level Domain (TLD) page, providing insights into TLD popularity, traffic, and security. The top-ranking TLD may come as a surprise.
articles.title: From .com to .anything: introducing Top-Level Domain (TLD) insights on Cloudflare Radar

articles.author: Marwan Fayed
articles.description: While large cloud providers hold vast troves of passive network data, analyzing them is complicated. The scale, noise, and absence of definitive ground truth all create major hurdles. Yet by carefully quantifying these constraints and finding alternative forms of evidence, meaningful insights can still emerge.
articles.title: Data at Cloudflare scale: some insights on measurement for 1,111 interns

articles.author: David Belson
articles.description: Cloudflare Radar has evolved significantly since its 2020 launch, offering deeper insights into Internet security, routing, and traffic with new tools and data that help anyone understand what's happening online.
articles.title: Making the Internet observable: the evolution of Cloudflare Radar
